notes.title: Dinodrifters News - #4: Upon New Shores
notes.content:
Hello, travellers of time and space!

Since the last news update, there have been several sub-updates - these were entirely focused on making bug-fixes to the Story Mode campaign, however, the content meat is yet to come.

It's been a while, but now it's time to discuss the upcoming v1.3.0 update to Dinodrifters.

Firstly, the v1.3.0 update will address some vital bugs that have been reported to me - the biggest one, the occasional crash at game start, will be addressed. I know what the issue is and it's close to being fixed - I ask only for a little more time to get this out there and working well.

As for gameplay features, there will be some tasty new content in v1.3.0. The most exciting of which are the two new maps to play on!

One is Cuddie Springs of Australia, 0.04 mya. It'll be a mammal-focused map featuring unique megafauna and geological traps. It's shaping up to be quite an interesting time and place to play in!

The second is going to be a new Mesozoic map, focused on of course, more dinosaurs! More on this when v1.3.0 comes closer to release.

As for the time of release, for now, I cannot say. It's coming, for sure, but I cannot give a date. I'm aiming for a release date before the end of Summer (Late August), and I'll do my best to achieve that. Worst comes to worst, I'll release the bug fixes and one of the maps instead, but I'd love to release with the two, though. Here's hoping!

Thanks for your time!

See you... out there!

- Jake

notes.title: Dinodrifters News - #3: Beyond Boundaries
notes.content:
Nos da, drifters! Or bore da, if it's sun-up where you are!

The new v1.2.0 update is out! Coming with over 100 new animals, a whole new area to explore and over 50 playable species, I hope you have fun with the new stuff! I know I had fun making it! It comes with a few bug fixes too. See the changelog in the update itself for the full details. For note, the new map, as will any future maps, be purple on the Time Select screen, to denote its post-release/update status.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36101526/56d97e7c8d62dd875a62a8ff4718073a6a0f0315.png[/img]

Today, I'd like to talk about what I plan to do next.

I've mentioned in previous posts that I'm working on a free game to come this year. That game is called Missy's Transformation Tournament. As of writing this, the plan is for it to release on Steam around May. It's systems are based on Dinodrifters', but the premise and gameplay are altogether different.

Whilst developing Missy's Transformation Tournament, I've expanded and polished the various things that first appeared in Dinodrifters - AI, programming, graphics - to fit an entirely different game. While both are RPGs, Dinodrifters is a turn-based wildlife survival game whilst Missy's Transformation Tournament is a real-time action battle royale game. However, the two games are compatible. They share the game base and mechanics.

In a nutshell: it's a real-time single-player battle royale RPG where you must transform your opponents into submission! Last contestant with their body and mind intact wins!

In addition, while Missy's Transformation Tournament is not a story-focused game, it is set in the same universe in which Dinodrifters takes place. Around 2300 years before the events of Dinodrifters' present (barring the flashbacks, of course). It focuses on the activities of Missy, a strange being with a link to one of the main characters of Dinodrifters (whom you meet in Episode 14). Though, I have to say, you would not want to meet her in a dark alley!

The plan for the next few months is to develop, release and get feedback from Missy's Transformation Tournament. After that, with only a little bit of tweaking, the upgraded systems from that game may be ported over, allowing for full 1920x1080 gameplay, an expanded view screen and improved AI capabilities!

However, none of this will happen soon. Definitely not before Missy's Transformation Tournament comes out. I can't promise any of this, but it's something I'd like to do if I get the chance.

Expect to see Missy's Transformation Tournament's Steam page in the coming weeks!

Well, enjoy the new update and have fun, everyone!

Make the most of your days!

- Jake

notes.title: Dinodrifters v1.2.0 Update
notes.content:
Version 1.2.0 of Dinodrifters has landed! The update will automatically download and install itself now.

Details:

A new gatemark has been unlocked! Explore the Judith River Formation of North America, based on a selection of Late Cretaceous fossil sites! A lush volcanic land home to a vast menagerie of animals both big and small! Playable both in Free and Story Mode!

Changelog:

[list]
[*] Added the Judith River Formation as a playable area!
[*] Added over 100 new animals, including over 50 new playable species!
[*] Added Judith River Formation as an option in the Time Select screen
[*] Added Judith River Formation for play in Story Mode
[*] Tweaked spawning mechanics for all maps
[*] Fixed a bug that made character names for male characters disappear in Story Mode
[*] Fixed a bug with events that made the drawn buttons not correlate to the actual buttons
[/list]

Hope fun out there, drifters!

- Jake

notes.title: Dinodrifters News - #1: Next Year Forward
notes.content:
Happy New Year everyone!

I hope you've had a good time since the last update! I had a great end of 2019; here's to 2020 being even better.

Now, though, it is time to return to regular development.

I'd like to talk about the plan for the upcoming February update to Dinodrifters.

It will be v1.2.0. and will come with a lot of new content not seen yet in the base game. While this is subject to change as development goes forward, I feel comfortable in telling you what to expect next month.

v1.2.0. will feature:

[list] [*] A new region based on the [i]Judith River Formation[/i] of Alberta, North America [76 Mya], as well as several contemporary adjacent sources. This new region will have new terrain, landscapes and features to explore!
[*] Dozens of new animal species to inhabit the new region, featuring Dromaeosaurus, Albertosaurus, Parasaurolophus, Corythosaurus and Deinosuchus! The total amount will be no less than 40, but probably more still than that!
[*] Updates to all existing maps, in particular the coding of the extremely small animals such as bugs and fish, will be changed to make them appear more often and lively.
[*] Graphical upgrades to the landscape and horizon system to vary the appearance of several maps more.
[/list]

This update is currently under development and is planned to come out sometime in February. I'll update you all with a concrete date as soon as possible.

That's what will come in the near future. However, I do have plans beyond February. In particular, I have several regions I'd love to make and I consider a high priority. While I cannot say when they will come, the following are maps I am considering adding in the coming months, in no particular order:

[list] [*] Kayenta Formation - Arizona, Early Jurassic - 193 Mya, home of Dilophosaurus
[*] Santa Maria Formation - Brazil, Late Triassic - 240 Mya
[*] Wessex Formation - England, Early Cretaceous - 130 Mya
[*] Camadas de Guimarotai - Portugal, Late Jurassic - 150 Mya, home of Compsognathus
[*] Central Europe Formation - Switzerland, Late Triassic - 230 Mya, home of Cymbospondylus, Nothosaurus and Tanystropheus
[*] Noibrara Formation- Nebraska, Late Cretaceous - 83 Mya, home of Tylosaurus, Archelon and Xiphactinus
[*] Qasr el Sagha - Egypt, Early Paleogene - 36 Mya, home of Basilosaurus and Andrewsarchus
[*] Great Rift Valley - Ethiopia, Late Paleogene – 3.3 Mya, home of Odobenocetops, Dinofelis, Deinotherium and Megalodon
[*] Lecho Formation - Argentina, Late Cretaceous - 70 Mya, home of Saltasaurus and Carnotaurus
[*] Hateg Island - Romania, Late Cretaceous - 70 Mya, home of many small, dwarf species of animals
[*] Cedar Mountain Formation - Utah, Early Cretaceous – 115 Mya, home of Acrocanthosaurus and Deinonychus 
[/list]

Bare in mind, through, that I cannot promise that these will come for sure this year, but these are the regions I am seriously considering adding. Let me know if there's any here that sound particularly enticing!

For now, Judith River comes first.

There are some upgrades to current gameplay systems I'd like to make, too. Especially to improve underwater and aerial gameplay. Maybe if I get to make some of the above regions, I'll bundle the update will some of these upgrades. We'll see.

Well, that just about covers it for this update.

I won't be posting news every week like I did during Early Access going forward. More of when I feel like I have something to share, be it an update, thought or plan.

Have a great 2020, everybody!

- Jake

notes.title: Dinodrifters Early Access News - Week #4: v1.1.0 Update
notes.content:
Merry Christmas! The first big update to Dinodrifters is here!

First of all, we are leaving Early Access on December 21st, so this version is the release version. I was going to wait to release it later, but I worked ahead of schedule and wanted to share it with you all.

I've finished Time Anomalies! They're a brand new feature that I have previously said would come in January, but I've moved it forward. I underestimated how quickly I would have it done, basically, so you get the release and January update in one! This version is called v.1.1.0 and will update automatically based on your Steam preferences.


v1.1.0 Changelog:

- Added Time Anomalies, portals through time that allow you and other animals to travel one-way between two different maps. When toggled at game start, an anomaly can only spawn when the player is an adult and has a 1% probability of doing so per turn. Anomalies will spawn an appropriate animal every 25 turns. A time anomaly has a 25% chance of disappearing when spawning an animal. Multiple anomalies can be active at any one time.
- Added Time Anomaly button to Free Mode selection screen. You must toggle this to play with Time Anomalies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36101526/518108c7d5106d093a702114300ff17228e21f29.png[/img]

- Fixed save error when playing a scenario, where certain events didn't trigger.
- Fixed text alignment issues on certain game menus.
- Fixed spawning issue with terrestrial animals in the Ordovician.
- Removed Early Access text on Main Menu screen.


Now, bare in mind, that at the moment, I have no additional plans in January for Dinodrifters. This was done early, mostly because I have another game I want to work on (a free one that will come out in the coming months). I'm currently thinking, that I work on that in January and in February, I'll add a new region into Dinodrifters, with several dozen new dinosaurs!

More details on that will come after Christmas, though, in the post-Early Access news updates to come. There'll be no updates for a while until sometime in January as I take a Christmas break.

Until then, Merry Christmas, everyone! I hope you have a great time! Remember to stay warm and appreciate all those you have in life. Family, friends, loved ones. It's the end of a decade and the beginning of sometime new. Time for new thoughts, new feelings, new ideas.

It's time... to transform.

See you next year and may the Drift keep you safe!

- Jake

notes.title: Dinodrifters Early Access News - Week #3: Time Anomalies
notes.content:
Another week down and just one more to go until we leave Early Access! What a ride!

Today, I want to talk about an upcoming feature that will come in January, after we leave Early Access. I want to talk about Time Anomalies.

Anomalies are portals through time and space that connect two different regions to one another. Their appearance is strange. Maybe they are related to the travellers in time, the Dinodrifters, operating the Timegate in the Quaternary?

To put it simply, they will appear in Free Mode and allow you to travel from your starting region to a new one in another time. Think of it as a fresh start. Not enjoying playing a Velociraptor in the Flaming Cliffs? Maybe move to the region through the anomaly!

In addition to the player, Time Anomalies will allow creatures, based on its destination region, to travel from the other side and enter your time. Mammoths can appear in the Triassic, Tyrannosaurus in the Cambrian, Liopleurodon in the Devonian. Any combination you can think of will be possible!

Don't worry about the prehistorical context! This feature must be selected at a game's start to work. If you want a more accurate experience, then simply do not toggle it.

Even when toggled, they are rare. They won't appear often. Maybe once every two average games. However, it will be possible to have more than one at once. Things will be very crazy if that should happen!

Dinodrifters leaves Early Access on December 21st, 2019, with the first new content update coming later, in January.

May the Drift keep you safe!

- Jake

notes.title: Dinodrifters Early Access News - Week #2: Out of the Past, Into the Future
notes.content:
Hope you're all having a blast playing Dinodrifters!

This week, I want to talk specifically about leaving Early Access.

From the feedback I've received, no game-breaking or otherwise massive bugs have been found. Yay!

However, I have identified several pieces of code and some oddities that will be corrected next update. They're mostly little things, like text slightly misaligned in some screens, a slight change in saving mechanics, that sort of thing. Your old saves will work fine, though, don't worry! The advantage of making your own save system is that you can definitely say what will break it. This will not!

However, all that being said, I see no reason to stay in Early Access for much longer.

I did so because a release of this scale is so new to me that I felt I needed some leeway regarding possible bugs and whatnot. Well, that was overcautiousness on my part!

As a result, Dinodrifters will leave Early Access [b]December 21st, 2019[/b]. On the same day, an update containing v1.1.0 of the game will be released, in answer to the affecting issues above.

Your game will replace the game with the new one, depending on your Steam settings, but if you want to keep the old version of the game, feel free to copy the game .exe from the Dinodrifters Steam file and keep it for your own personal use. I don't mind and it should work without Steam (no achievements or save cloud use though).

Well, that's it for this week, then! Have a great day, everyone!

May the Drift keep you safe!

- Jake

notes.title: Dinodrifters Early Access News - Week #1: The Road Ahead
notes.content:
Hello all you newly joined Dinodrifters out there!

Welcome to the first newsletter of Dinodrifters' Early Access period.

So much has happened in this last week! The amount of interest Dinodrifters has attained has warmed my heart greatly. However, this is only the beginning! Dinodrifters is going to receiving an update in December fixing the known bugs that have since been identified.

Once that is done, as long as no other surprises are brought to light, then Dinodrifters is going to release fully in December, just before Christmas, hopefully.

Further down the road, I plan to add several new areas/regions in the game based on further fossil sites. While this is subject to change, my current plan is to add the Judith River Formation, home of Parasaurolophus and Albertosaurus, as a playable map and add a new gameplay feature: time anomalies.

Time anomalies are portals that can randomly spawn in during a game of Free Mode and allow animals to players and other animals to travel to a different map entirely. This will be toggleable at game start and allow players to leave their map for a new destination one, making them surely one-of-a-kind in that region! Time anomalies will passively spawn animals from its assigned destination region over time. Imagine a Tyrannosaurus hunting a Mammoth!

That update should come after Dinodrifters is out of Early Access.

That's all for this week! Enjoy Dinodrifters and make sure to uncover the plot of those dreaded Rogues!

May the Drift keep you safe!

- Jake
